summary: Intro demo of Redwood Hosted API for chat and text generation. Focused on streaming, request params, retry behavior, and integration considerations for PHI-sensitive workflows. Customer wants low latency and predictable cost; security team asked about KMS/SOC2, data retention, and VPC options.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood Inference. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Maya Thompson: Maya here, head of data at Willow Health.
[00:10] Liam Brooks: Liam, eng manager.
[00:12] Ava Chen: Ava from security.
[00:15] Claire: Claire, I'm the solutions eng, hi.
[00:18] Samir: Great, thanks. Agenda is quick product tour of the Hosted API for chat/text, show streaming, param tuning, retries, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:32] Liam: Good, we're especially focused on latency for interactive clinical workflows and cost per 1k tokens, so want to see how Redwood handles that.
[00:40] Samir: Totally, we'll call out batching, KV cache and price tradeoffs. Claire will demo the console and SDK.
[00:48] Claire: Ok sharing screen - uh small note, sharing says "Redwood Console v2" at top, ignore the demo data.
[00:56] Claire: Walk through the APIs - start with a simple chat request, here's the cURL: POST /v1/chat/completions with model param, messages, and stream=true to get server-sent events.
[01:12] Maya: Quick question - is stream implemented as SSE? We run node and python clients.
[01:16] Claire: Yes SSE for text streaming, and SDKs wrap it so you get chunk callbacks. There's also websocket beta. Some transcriptions here call it "Redwood Stream" but it's just SSE under the hood.
[01:29] [minor crosstalk] Noah: And how's partial token billing shown?
[01:33] Samir: Billing is per token emitted, we show token breakdown in Console per request and you can view latency per token.
[01:40] Claire: Demo: set temperature at 0.2 for deterministic clinical summaries, top_p fine tuning, and max_tokens guardrails. Watch the stream come in - chunk1, chunk2 - slight pause then final.
[01:58] Liam: If we stream smaller chunks more frequently, do we get higher latency or any penalty?
[02:03] Claire: Slight CPU overhead but negligible on hosted infra, the main cost is network RTT. We recommend batching client-side for throughput but streaming for interactive UIs.
[02:15] Ava: Security - when request contains PHI, does Redwood persist prompts or is it configurable?
[02:21] Samir: Hosted defaults to short retention but for PHI customers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; we have retention flags and you can opt out of logging. We'll share SOC2 docs.
[02:34] Ava: KMS? We need BYOK and HSM options.
[02:38] Rosa: We integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated, for Hosted we have managed keys but offer customer-managed keys on higher tiers. I'll include the KMS note in the security pack.
[02:49] Claire: Back to retries: we show typical retry pattern in SDKs - idempotency_key on request, exponential backoff with jitter, and server 429 includes retry-after.
[02:59] Liam: If a request partially completes and client retries, how do we avoid double-charges?
[03:04] Claire: Use idempotency_key - the API ensures at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics depending on model and caching. For streaming we write partial events but the SDK reconciles. I'll send the exact semantics doc - it's in the link at the top.
[03:18] Maya: Can we pin model versions? We need stable output for regulatory validations.
[03:22] Samir: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies in Console, plus A/B and canary. We also do model variant fallbacks if capacity constrained.
[03:30] Claire: Quick demo of Console: route rules, per-model latency dashboards, and Optimize suggestions - it suggests batching sizes and quantization for cost.
[03:44] Noah: About Optimize - is that automatic or advisory?
[03:47] Rosa: Advisory - it analyzes traces and suggests settings; some options are auto-apply for Dedicated pools but Hosted is advisory.
[03:56] Liam: For benching we want a script to replay our traffic with same sequence length and key distribution.
[04:01] Claire: We have a benchmarking harness and a sample harness repo. We'll run a pilot bench with your traffic profile.
[04:08] Maya: Any hard SLAs for hosted latency?
[04:11] Samir: Hosted is non-SLA for standard, but Dedicated has SLA-backed latency. Hosted typical p95 for chat is ~200-400ms token-to-token depending on model. We can share our perf spreadsheet.
[04:28] Ava: Compliance - need audit logs and RBAC for console admin.
[04:32] Rosa: Console supports SSO, SAML, RBAC roles, and audit logs export. We'll include screenshots.
[04:40] Liam: Integrations - we run on k8s, will we need a sidecar?
[04:44] Claire: No sidecar for Hosted; for Private we provide deployment package and operator. Hosted integrates via REST/SDK.
[04:51] [pause]
[04:56] Samir: Ok quick recap and next steps - we'll send pilot pricing and a 3-month plan, security pack, and schedule the pilot kickoff + benchmark session. Who will be the primary contact?
[05:08] Liam: I can be technical lead for the pilot, Maya will owner validation, Ava will own security signoff.
[05:15] Samir: Great - action items captured in the calendar invite. Anything else?
[05:19] Maya: One last - do you have examples of prompt QA and evals for clinical outputs?
[05:23] Claire: Yes we have an evals harness and can share sample prompt sets, plus regression alerts in Optimize.
[05:30] Noah: Cool thanks for the demo.
[05:33] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[05:36] [end]
